newsitem.title: USA: G7 leaders say must do more to help world economy.
newsitem.headline: G7 leaders say must do more to help world economy.

text.p: Leaders of the Group of Seven industrial nations on Saturday welcomed signs of an improving world economy but said more needed to be done to ensure that the good times continued and that everyone benefited.
In a draft of a statement to be issued later on Saturday, the leaders also set out specific economic goals for their countries to help ensure that global expansion remains on track.

"We have been encouraged by the many positive indicators in our economies," the G7 countries of Britain, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan and the United States, said. "But we still have work to do in our own economies."

The leaders urged their finance ministers to work together and to cooperate closely in currency markets to help promote international monetary stability. They also welcomed efforts by the European Union to forge a single currency but stressed that it must be backed up by sound economic policies.

In setting out specific goals for each nation, the G7 said the United States needed to guard against a resurgence of inflation and follow through with efforts to balance the government budget. Japan must rely on domestic demand, not on exports, for faster economic growth and avoid a big rise in its trade surplus, they said.

France, Germany and Italy, all of which are plagued by sky-high unemployment, needed to restructure their economies to promote job creation. Britain must keep inflation in check and cut its budget deficit further. As for Canada, it has enjoyed faster economic growth recently that should reduce joblessness, the G7 said.
